transcript: It's my sinuses. I've had facial pressure and headaches behind my eyes for over a year now.
Have you been treated for it?
So many times — like four rounds of antibiotics and a steroid spray. Nothing helps for long.
They did a CT and said it looked basically normal, which was frustrating.
And lately I've been getting really dizzy too — kind of spinning, it comes and goes and lasts a while.
Tell me more about the dizziness.
Bright lights and busy places make it worse — grocery store aisles, scrolling on my phone. And my ear feels full and rings when it happens.
My mom had migraines, if that matters.
Has anyone looked into the dizziness?
They didn't find anything wrong. One doctor said it was probably just anxiety and stress.
I've seen three or four different doctors about all of this.

ph: light bothers me during the spell

r_dur.q: This has been going on — or keeps coming back — for more than 3 months.

r_abx.q: I've had two or more rounds of antibiotics or steroids and they didn't fix it for long.

r_surg.q: I've had sinus surgery or a procedure, and the symptoms came back.

r_lesion.q: I get dizzy spells or ear symptoms, and nobody has found a cause.

r_normal.q: My scans or exams came back normal, or close to normal, even though I feel bad.
r_normal.ask: What exactly did my previous scans and exams show?

m_head.q: How often do you get headaches, or pressure and pain across your face and cheeks?

m_dur.ask: How long does an untreated episode usually last? I'm not certain.
m_dur.q: If you don't treat it, how long does one episode usually last?

m_photo.q: Light or noise bothers me more than usual during an episode.

m_nausea.q: I feel sick to my stomach during an episode.

m_disable.q: Episodes stop me doing things I'd normally do.

m_aura.q: Before or during an episode I see spots, zigzags or flashing lights — or I get numbness or tingling.

m_trig.q: Certain things set it off — weather changes, poor sleep, skipping meals, or my period.

m_fhx.q: I get migraines, or someone in my family does.

v_vertigo.q: When you get a dizzy or spinning spell, how long does it last?

v_count.q: I've had at least five of these spells.

v_migfeat.q: At least half of my spells come with a headache, or with light and noise bothering me.
v_migfeat.ask: Should I be tracking whether my spells come with headache or light sensitivity?

v_motion.q: Busy patterns, scrolling on a screen, or riding in a car make me feel off.

v_aural.q: My ears feel full, or ring, when the spells happen.

v_head.q: Moving my head or changing position brings it on.

n_burn.q: I get burning, tingling or shooting feelings in my face, mouth or throat.

n_otalgia.q: I get deep ear or throat pain, but my ear was checked and looked fine.

n_auto.q: I get dry eyes or a dry mouth, lightheadedness when I stand up, sweating changes, or stomach trouble.
n_auto.ask: Could dryness, lightheadedness and stomach changes be connected to this?

n_viral.q: All of this started after I was sick with a virus.

n_allo.q: A light touch, or normal pressure, hurts more than it should.

i_days.q: How many days a month does this affect you?

i_role.q: How much does it get in the way of work, school or home life?

x_purulent.q: During a flare I've had thick coloured drainage, or a swab grew an infection.
x_purulent.ask: During a flare, did I ever have thick coloured drainage, or a swab that grew an infection?
x_purulent.help: This is one your notes may answer. "Not sure" is a fine answer.

x_objective.q: A scan or a camera test showed real sinus swelling while I was having symptoms.
x_objective.ask: Did any of my scans or scope tests show real sinus swelling while I had symptoms?
x_objective.help: Look for words like sinusitis, mucosal thickening, or opacification on a CT report.

x_lowfreq.q: A hearing test showed my hearing drops during spells and comes back afterwards.
x_lowfreq.ask: Do my hearing tests show my hearing changing between visits?
x_lowfreq.help: This means two hearing tests at different times, not one.

x_anosmia.q: My sense of smell is reduced or gone, even between flares.
x_anosmia.ask: Has my sense of smell been formally tested?

rf_thunderclap.q: A headache that went from nothing to the worst pain within about a minute.
rf_thunderclap.say: I had a headache that reached its worst point within a minute.

rf_focal.q: New weakness, numbness, slurred speech, trouble swallowing, or double vision that doesn't go away.
rf_focal.say: I have new weakness, numbness, speech trouble or double vision.

rf_vision.q: Losing vision, or my vision greying out or dimming — even for a few seconds.
rf_vision.say: I'm having episodes where my vision greys out or dims.

rf_gca.q: I'm over 50 and my scalp is tender, or my jaw aches when I chew.
rf_gca.say: I'm over 50 with a tender scalp and jaw pain when I chew. I'd like blood tests today.

rf_orbital.q: Swelling around my eye, my eye bulging, eye pain, or trouble moving my eye.
rf_orbital.say: I have swelling around my eye and trouble moving it.

rf_ssnhl.q: My hearing dropped suddenly — over a few hours or a day — in the last month.
rf_ssnhl.say: My hearing dropped suddenly. I'd like a hearing test today, not in a few weeks.

rf_asym.q: My hearing loss or ringing is always in the same one ear.
rf_asym.say: My hearing loss and ringing are only ever in one ear, and I'd like that looked into.

rf_pulsatile.q: The ringing pulses along with my heartbeat.
rf_pulsatile.say: My ear noise pulses in time with my heartbeat.

rf_progressive.q: My headache is steadily getting worse, or it's worse when I wake up, cough, strain or lie flat.
rf_progressive.say: My headaches are getting worse and are worst when I lie down or wake up.

rf_new50.q: This is the first time in my life I've had headaches like this, and I'm over 50.
rf_new50.say: These are the first severe headaches of my life and I'm over 50.

rf_mass.q: One side of my nose is blocked with bleeding, or my cheek has gone numb.
rf_mass.say: One side of my nose is blocked and bleeding, and my cheek is numb.

rf_systemic.q: Fevers, night sweats, or weight I didn't mean to lose.
rf_systemic.say: I've had night sweats and unexplained weight loss alongside this.

c_clin.q: How many different clinicians have you seen about this?

c_dur.q: How long has this been going on?

c_dismiss.q: Have you been told it's stress or anxiety, or that everything looks normal?

story.title: Your story
story.heading: Your story so far
story.lede: This part matters more than people expect. How long you've been at this, and how many doors you've already knocked on, changes what a good next step looks like.
story.intro: A few things about what's been tried already.

migraine.title: Headache pattern
migraine.lede: Migraine doesn't always mean a classic headache. It can show up as pressure across the face and cheeks that feels exactly like a sinus problem.

vestibular.title: Dizziness and ears
vestibular.lede: Dizziness and ear symptoms can come from the same mechanism, even when hearing tests and scans are normal.

neuro.title: Nerve-type symptoms
neuro.lede: Some people get nerve-type symptoms — burning, tingling, or pain that doesn't match what an exam shows.

impact.title: Daily impact
impact.lede: Two quick questions. These tend to carry a lot of weight with clinicians, so it's worth being accurate rather than brave.

discriminators.title: Test results
discriminators.lede: These point away from the pattern this tool looks for, which makes them just as useful. Plenty of people won't know — "Not sure" is genuinely the right answer then.

ui.sub: A MASQUE tool · for people with ongoing sinus, ear or dizziness problems
forYouIf: You've had sinus, face-pressure, ear or dizziness symptoms for months.
Treatments haven't held, or your scans came back normal and you still feel unwell.
You've seen more than one clinician about it.
ui.clinicianLede: Patient-reported features, MASQUE instrument v{instrument}. Self-reported and not a screening result — no index was calculated. Items marked **−** point away from the migrainous/neuropathic pattern.

r_dur.q: Esto lleva más de 3 meses, o vuelve una y otra vez.

r_abx.q: He tomado dos o más ciclos de antibióticos o esteroides y no lo resolvieron por mucho tiempo.

r_surg.q: Me operaron de los senos nasales o me hicieron un procedimiento, y los síntomas volvieron.

r_lesion.q: Me dan mareos o síntomas del oído, y nadie ha encontrado la causa.

r_normal.q: Mis estudios o exámenes salieron normales, o casi normales, aunque me siento mal.
r_normal.ask: ¿Qué mostraron exactamente mis estudios y exámenes anteriores?

m_head.q: ¿Con qué frecuencia le dan dolores de cabeza, o presión y dolor en la cara y los pómulos?

m_dur.q: Si no lo trata, ¿cuánto dura normalmente un episodio?
m_dur.ask: ¿Cuánto dura un episodio sin tratar? No estoy seguro.

m_photo.q: La luz o el ruido me molestan más de lo normal durante un episodio.

m_nausea.q: Siento náuseas o malestar del estómago durante un episodio.

m_disable.q: Los episodios me impiden hacer cosas que normalmente haría.

m_aura.q: Antes o durante un episodio veo puntos, líneas en zigzag o luces destellantes — o siento entumecimiento u hormigueo.

m_trig.q: Ciertas cosas lo provocan — cambios de clima, dormir mal, saltarme comidas, o mi periodo.

m_fhx.q: Me dan migrañas, o alguien de mi familia las tiene.

v_vertigo.q: Cuando le da un episodio de mareo o de que todo da vueltas, ¿cuánto dura?

v_count.q: He tenido al menos cinco de estos episodios.

v_migfeat.q: Por lo menos la mitad de mis episodios vienen con dolor de cabeza, o con molestia por la luz y el ruido.
v_migfeat.ask: ¿Debería anotar si mis episodios vienen con dolor de cabeza o molestia por la luz?

v_motion.q: Los patrones muy cargados, deslizar la pantalla, o ir en el carro me hacen sentir mal.

v_aural.q: Siento los oídos tapados, o me zumban, cuando me dan los episodios.

v_head.q: Mover la cabeza o cambiar de posición me lo provoca.

n_burn.q: Siento ardor, hormigueo o punzadas en la cara, la boca o la garganta.

n_otalgia.q: Me duele hondo el oído o la garganta, pero me revisaron el oído y estaba bien.

n_auto.q: Se me secan los ojos o la boca, me mareo al pararme, sudo distinto, o tengo problemas del estómago.
n_auto.ask: ¿La resequedad, el mareo al pararme y los cambios del estómago podrían estar relacionados con esto?

n_viral.q: Todo esto empezó después de que me enfermé de un virus.

n_allo.q: Un roce suave, o una presión normal, me duele más de lo que debería.

i_days.q: ¿Cuántos días al mes le afecta esto?

i_role.q: ¿Qué tanto le estorba en el trabajo, la escuela o la casa?

x_purulent.q: Durante una crisis he tenido flujo espeso y de color, o un cultivo salió con infección.
x_purulent.ask: Durante una crisis, ¿alguna vez tuve flujo espeso de color, o un cultivo con infección?
x_purulent.help: Esta puede estar en su expediente. "No estoy seguro" es una buena respuesta.

x_objective.q: Un estudio o una cámara mostró inflamación real de los senos nasales mientras yo tenía síntomas.
x_objective.ask: ¿Alguno de mis estudios mostró inflamación real de los senos nasales cuando tenía síntomas?
x_objective.help: Busque palabras como sinusitis, engrosamiento de la mucosa u opacificación en un reporte de tomografía.

x_lowfreq.q: Una prueba de audición mostró que mi oído baja durante los episodios y luego regresa.
x_lowfreq.ask: ¿Mis pruebas de audición muestran cambios entre una visita y otra?
x_lowfreq.help: Esto significa dos pruebas en momentos distintos, no una sola.

x_anosmia.q: Mi sentido del olfato está disminuido o perdido, incluso entre crisis.
x_anosmia.ask: ¿Me han hecho una prueba formal del olfato?

rf_thunderclap.q: Un dolor de cabeza que pasó de nada al peor dolor en como un minuto.
rf_thunderclap.say: Tuve un dolor de cabeza que llegó a su punto más fuerte en menos de un minuto.

rf_focal.q: Debilidad nueva, entumecimiento, hablar arrastrado, dificultad para tragar, o ver doble y no se quita.
rf_focal.say: Tengo debilidad, entumecimiento, problemas para hablar o visión doble, y son nuevos.

rf_vision.q: Perder la vista, o que se me nuble u oscurezca la vista — aunque sea por segundos.
rf_vision.say: Estoy teniendo episodios en los que se me oscurece o se me nubla la vista.

rf_gca.q: Tengo más de 50 años y me duele el cuero cabelludo, o me duele la mandíbula al masticar.
rf_gca.say: Tengo más de 50 años, me duele el cuero cabelludo y la mandíbula al masticar. Quisiera análisis de sangre hoy.

rf_orbital.q: Hinchazón alrededor del ojo, el ojo saltado, dolor de ojo, o no poder moverlo bien.
rf_orbital.say: Tengo hinchazón alrededor del ojo y dificultad para moverlo.

rf_ssnhl.q: Mi audición bajó de repente — en unas horas o un día — en el último mes.
rf_ssnhl.say: Mi audición bajó de repente. Quisiera una prueba de audición hoy, no en unas semanas.

rf_asym.q: La pérdida de audición o el zumbido siempre es del mismo oído.
rf_asym.say: La pérdida de audición y el zumbido son solo de un oído, y quisiera que lo revisaran.

rf_pulsatile.q: El zumbido late al mismo ritmo que mi corazón.
rf_pulsatile.say: El ruido en mi oído late al ritmo de mi corazón.

rf_progressive.q: Mi dolor de cabeza va empeorando poco a poco, o es peor al despertar, toser, hacer fuerza o acostarme.
rf_progressive.say: Mis dolores de cabeza están empeorando y son peores cuando me acuesto o al despertar.

rf_new50.q: Es la primera vez en mi vida que me dan dolores de cabeza así, y tengo más de 50 años.
rf_new50.say: Estos son los primeros dolores de cabeza fuertes de mi vida y tengo más de 50 años.

rf_mass.q: Un lado de la nariz está tapado y sangra, o se me durmió el pómulo.
rf_mass.say: Un lado de mi nariz está tapado y sangrando, y tengo el pómulo dormido.

rf_systemic.q: Fiebres, sudores de noche, o peso que bajé sin querer.
rf_systemic.say: He tenido sudores nocturnos y he bajado de peso sin explicación.

migraine.title: Patrón de dolor de cabeza
migraine.lede: La migraña no siempre es un dolor de cabeza clásico. Puede aparecer como presión en la cara y los pómulos que se siente igual que un problema de los senos nasales.

vestibular.title: Mareos y oídos
vestibular.lede: Los mareos y los síntomas del oído pueden venir del mismo mecanismo, aunque las pruebas de audición y los estudios salgan normales.

neuro.title: Síntomas de los nervios
neuro.lede: Algunas personas tienen síntomas de los nervios — ardor, hormigueo, o dolor que no corresponde con lo que muestra el examen.

impact.title: Impacto diario
impact.lede: Dos preguntas rápidas. Estas suelen pesar mucho con los médicos, así que vale más ser exacto que valiente.

discriminators.title: Resultados de estudios
discriminators.lede: Estas apuntan en dirección contraria al patrón que busca esta herramienta, lo cual las hace igual de útiles. Mucha gente no lo sabrá — ahí "No estoy seguro" es de verdad la respuesta correcta.

demoCohorts.why: The §3.2 defect in data, plus divergent gender and a 6-row stratum. FAIL, so §11's gate withholds the model.

The weighted model is interpretable and illustrative, pending validation on the open-data sources named in the Project MASQUE proposal (NHANES, NHIS, MEPS, CMS, HCUP, openFDA, CDC, All of Us).
emrDetails: **Launch.** The app opens from the chart via a SMART on FHIR EHR launch; the patient banner above is populated from the launch context (here, a sandbox Patient resource).
**Capture.** The clinician or patient completes the short screen; nothing is sent anywhere while answering.
**Write-back.** Results post as FHIR resources — a QuestionnaireResponse, an Observation carrying the MASQUE index and band, and a conditional ServiceRequest for referral — shown in the bundle above.
**Prompt.** A CDS Hooks card surfaces the recommendation in the ordering workflow.
**Privacy.** In deployment, acoustic / free-text features are extracted at the edge and raw identifiable data is not centralized; codes shown here use a placeholder system and are illustrative.
screener.specIntro: These are generated from the running item set, so they cannot drift from the instrument the app actually scores with. The Questionnaire is what this screen's QuestionnaireResponse resources point at.

about: **Listen.** In this prototype the browser's own speech recognition transcribes the microphone (a deployment runs ambient ASR on-device); rule-based extraction maps what the patient says to MASQUE items as each phrase lands (shown as green capture tags — dashed while a phrase is still being recognised).

**Prompt.** The scribe computes coverage and surfaces only the highest-yield unasked questions for the active pathway — pulling in the VM-PATHI vestibular domains once otologic symptoms appear — so the physician asks what matters without reading a 25-item form aloud.

**Document.** Captured findings, the MASQUE index, and the plan assemble into a draft note and a FHIR bundle (QuestionnaireResponse, Observation, ServiceRequest, DocumentReference) for one-tap sign-off.
**Protect.** No raw audio is retained; only structured findings persist.

changelog.note: Extracted from the frozen baseline (app/tests/baseline/src, MANIFEST.sha256) by app/tests/tools/extract-rubric.html; field-by-field sources in modules/masque/SOURCES.md. Instrument 0.2 unchanged: item ids, weights, scale factors, cut-points and wording are moved, not edited.

Red flags take the canonical Screener wording (text, points, action). The Scribe's shortened copy and the Simulator's third variant are dropped; the Scribe's per-flag `ask` is kept as unread data (Q5, Q6).

Item text is canonical from the Screener (byte-identical to the Scribe's). The Scribe's ASK map becomes `ask`, its shortLabel map becomes `short` (n_allo has none, so the id is shown as today, Q24), VMPATHI_TAG becomes `tag`, and the Patient's clinician line `c` becomes `patientClin`. The Simulator's item copy (no scale factors, linear scoring) is dropped.

Patient context options keep the Patient's own values and labels (1/2/3+, <6mo/6-12mo/>12mo, no/yes); they are not realigned to the clinician bins (Q8). The gap-rule signal values (3+, >12mo, yes) are identical in both vocabularies.
The Patient ITEMS domain `label`/`clinical` fields (never read) are dropped; the patient step titles come from the Patient section titles (UI.sections).

The five Simulator scenarios are added as sample cases sim-empty, sim-partial, sim-high, sim-redflag and sim-ruleout (group "scenario", `why` kept as the button title, FULL_HIGH inlined, `step` dropped, no complaint) (Q3).

The research panel's PROJECTS.MASQUE entry moves to `research`, with the brand-named knobs (score alias, artifact key, ETL script, fairness axes) and the Simulator's demo cohorts as data. BREATHE and VOICED stay in the panel as panel-only projects.
Open questions shipped with their stated defaults: the label is display-only (Q1); the Scribe note keeps "Instrument v0.3 candidates." verbatim (Q7).
